title: Interpretable machine learning finds a promoter architecture marking Menin-KMT2A occupancy
summary: Interpretable machine learning identified a composite promoter architecture of CpG islands flanked by several-kilobase A/T-rich domains (AT-flanks) associated with high occupancy of the Menin-KMT2A complex at developmental and leukemia-associated genes. Genetic deletion and chromatin-contact analyses showed AT-flanks support KMT2A retention, and LEDGF was required for Menin engagement at them. AT-flank extent was associated with differential KMT2A loss after Menin-KMT2A inhibition. The abstract does not name the model type; only the abstract was reviewed.
ai_technology: Interpretable machine-learning model of promoter sequence features predicting Menin-KMT2A occupancy

evidence.tested: Genetic deletion, chromatin-contact analysis and pharmacologic disruption of Menin-KMT2A.
evidence.unknown: Model type, performance and how much of the result rests on ML versus experiments; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: The interpretable model highlighted the AT-flank architecture that was then tested experimentally.
